question_text: The activation energy for the diffusion of copper in silver is 193,000 J/mol. Calculate the diffusion coefficient at $1200 \mathrm{~K}\left(927^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$, given that $D$ at $1000 \mathrm{~K}\left(727^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ is $1.0 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{s}$.The unit of the answer is m^2/s.
response:
Using the Arrhenius relation in ratio form,

$$\frac{D_2}{D_1}=\exp\!\left[-\frac{Q_d}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_2}-\frac{1}{T_1}\right)\right]$$

with $Q_d=193000\ \text{J/mol}$, $R=8.31\ \text{J/mol·K}$, $T_1=1000\ \text{K}$, $T_2=1200\ \text{K}$, and $D_1=1.0\times10^{-14}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$:

$$D_2 = 1.0\times10^{-14}\exp\!\left[-\frac{193000}{8.31}\left(\frac{1}{1200}-\frac{1}{1000}\right)\right]\approx 4.8\times10^{-13}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$$

$$\boxed{4.8\times10^{-13}}$$
